value.title: PRD 004: Hub layouts
value.summary: The graph view gives nodes real room and lets the operator choose a natural layout or an Obsidian-style fan around hubs found by connections, similarity or graph rules. Initial modes, hub selection, controls and reproducible free-layout fans are delivered; complete spacing, spine, interaction and performance acceptance evidence remains in progress. Rule-provenance integration is deferred.

sections.name: why
sections.value:
Nodes still sit on top of one another even at maximum spacing, and the logical fan-out is not readable. The operator wants the shape of an Obsidian graph: hubs with their things fanned around them, while unrelated nodes are free to settle where their links take them.

The view already has force layout, spacing, similarity links and a spine with its own spread control. PR #71 kept a 747-node, 30-band spine from becoming a thin strip; PR #58 reduced per-graph fetch time from 1.9-13 seconds to 0.05-0.4 seconds. Hub layouts must keep those gains, not add a second round of graph reads or flatten a timeline into circles.

A layout hub is not always a declared hub. Degree and similarity suggest centres for a view. PRD 003 rules-15 and rules-18 define real hubs through fill rules and the filled_by provenance of their edges, which are not built yet. This PRD keeps that boundary visible and does not implement graph rules.

value.name: graph reader
value.need: See each node, understand which things gather around a hub, and switch layouts without losing the graph or its timeline.

value.goal: Nodes have room at sensible defaults, and spacing visibly increases that room.
Several hubs and their neighbours read as separate fans, with everything else free to settle by its links.
Every layout works with a spine or without one, and the same graph and settings give the same result.

value.text: The graph-rules engine, fill writes, a new hub node type, or any graph mutation to produce a layout. Those remain in PRD 003.
New embeddings, an all-pairs similarity calculation, a new daemon endpoint or a wire-format change. Any later need for new served data must be agreed separately.
Copying Obsidian's whole interface, replacing the renderer, or adding a graph-editing feature.
Showing every label at every zoom. Labels may be withheld when crowded; visible nodes must not be hidden to make the layout pass.

value.title: Choose a layout in the view
value.statement: A labelled, keyboard-accessible Layout control offers Normal, Degree hubs, Similarity hubs and Declared hubs. Similarity hubs is the initial choice. Degree hubs alone shows a sub-choice: Most incoming, Most outgoing or Most connections. The chosen mode, sub-choice and Hubs count survive a reload with the existing view settings, without putting graph names in the URL. The spine selector remains independent.
value.done_when: Using the keyboard, select each mode and each degree sub-choice, reload and get the same pick; selecting or clearing a spine does not change that pick, and selecting a layout does not change the spine pick.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (four layout modes); existing view-settings and spine behaviour

value.title: Normal follows links without forcing hubs
value.statement: Normal settles the graph from its edges without an imposed hub fan. Connected groups remain recognisable, disconnected groups do not pile together, and isolated nodes still get a place. It does not require similarity data, a spine or rules.
value.done_when: A synthetic graph with a star, a cycle, two disconnected groups and isolated nodes opens in Normal with every visible node placed, finite coordinates and no forced circular arrangement of every group.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (Normal is the best layout from edges alone)

value.title: Spacing gives real room in every mode
value.statement: No two distinct visible node glyphs overlap in a settled layout at the default spacing. Increasing Spacing increases their clearance at the same camera scale, accounting for the sizes actually drawn, rather than merely moving whole groups further apart. With a spine shown, Spread increases room within and between bands without undoing that clearance. Fit includes the outermost nodes, fans, spine and drawn labels; labels that are drawn do not overlap one another.
value.done_when: In every mode with the spine off and on, check a dense 1,000-node synthetic graph at default and maximum spacing: distinct glyphs have positive clearance, larger spacing increases within-group clearance at fixed zoom, visible labels do not overlap, and Fit clips no outer node or drawn label. Intentional entity merging is checked as one glyph, not as overlapping hidden members.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (maximum spacing still overlaps); PR #71 (spine clearance and Fit)

value.title: Degree hubs follow the chosen direction
value.statement: Degree hubs ranks candidate centres by distinct incoming neighbours, distinct outgoing neighbours or distinct neighbours in either direction, as selected. When similarity data exists, degree receives a bounded boost favouring nodes central to their similarity cluster; without it, ranking is plain degree. Self-links do not count and parallel links to the same neighbour count once. Up to the chosen Hubs count are selected, with stable node-id tie-breaks, and their visible immediate neighbours fan around them.
value.done_when: Without similarity data, a directed fixture has different leaders for incoming, outgoing and total connections; each sub-choice puts the appropriate leader at its fan's centre. Self-links and duplicate parallel links change none of those counts, and tied candidates are ordered by stable id. With similarity data, an equally connected node central to its cluster is preferred.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (most incoming, outgoing or connections; centrality preference)
value.note: The approved ranking is degree multiplied by 1 plus up to 25% of normalised within-cluster similarity centrality. Nodes need at least two distinct neighbours to be useful centres.

value.title: Similarity hubs use the similarity already available
value.statement: Similarity hubs forms clusters from the available similar_to links and served similarity data, not from ordinary structural links alone. Each cluster fans around its most central member: the greatest total within-cluster similarity weight, with equal-weight links when no numeric score is available and stable id as the tie-break. No embedding or new similarity computation is requested for a layout. Nodes outside those clusters remain free.
value.done_when: A fixture with two similarity clusters and a structurally high-degree outsider centres each cluster on its highest within-cluster similarity total, not on the outsider; an unscored similar_to fixture also works. With no similarity links or usable similarity data, the mode falls back to Degree hubs using Most connections and shows a small note saying so, with no embedder or extra similarity request.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (central member of a similarity cluster; reuse daemon data; plain-degree fallback)

value.title: Declared mode has an honest part_of preview
value.statement: Until rule provenance is available to the view, Declared hubs uses nodes with at least two distinct incoming part_of neighbours as candidate centres and fans those children around their parent. The control explains that this is an inferred part_of preview, not proof of a fill rule. With no candidates it says so and leaves nodes in Normal positions. The preview creates no rules or edges.
value.done_when: In a fixture with parent nodes, part_of children and unrelated outgoing edges, the preview centres parents and fans only their children; outgoing part_of links and duplicate edges do not invent a hub. The UI identifies the preview and handles a graph with no candidate without hiding nodes.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (incoming part_of fallback until PRD 003 slice 3)
value.note: The initial UI delivery uses this preview; hub-07 is the later provenance-aware integration.

value.title: Real declared hubs use fill provenance when available
value.statement: When the view can read PRD 003's fill-rule provenance, Declared hubs recognises the rule's named target as an ordinary hub node and its incoming part_of edges carrying filled_by as membership, without inferring membership from degree or node type. The same layout mode and spine behaviour remain. A node may belong to several declared hubs without being duplicated on screen.
value.done_when: After rules-15 and rules-18 are delivered and their data is available to the view, a fixture distinguishes filled part_of edges from manual ones, recognises a declared hub with one member, and preserves a shared member as one selectable node with all its edges.
value.source: PRD 003 rules-15, rules-18; project lead 2026-11-26 (real declared hubs)
value.note: Deferred until PRD 003's rules slice 3 and any separately agreed data exposure; not an initial UI delivery gate.

value.title: Fans do not swallow the rest of the graph
value.statement: With the spine off, a hub's neighbours form a circle or concentric rings with room for their glyphs; a crowded fan grows rather than stacking its members. Several hubs remain separate, and unrelated nodes settle by force rather than being assigned to an arbitrary hub. A shared neighbour has one stable primary fan assignment and keeps every real edge, including links to other hubs; nested hubs and cycles do not duplicate nodes.
value.done_when: Show fixtures with a high-degree star, two hubs sharing neighbours, a hub linked to another hub, a cycle and isolates. Fans have no glyph overlap, the shared neighbour is drawn and selectable once, all its links remain, and the isolates are not forced into a ring.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (circular fans, other nodes free)

value.title: The spine's order wins over a fan
value.statement: Every layout works with the selected spine shown or hidden. When shown, anchor and band order along the spine's axis takes precedence: a fan stays within a member's own band and may be clipped into arcs or multiple rings rather than pulling that member to the hub's band. Anchors remain on the axis; unplaced nodes remain on the unplaced shelf. Turning the spine off restores the chosen layout, not an unrelated mode.
value.done_when: For every mode on a two-spine fixture, switch between spines and None. A hub with neighbours in earlier and later bands never reverses or changes their band order, crowded bands and the shelf stay clear, and None restores that mode's reproducible non-spine layout.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (spine order wins along its axis); PR #71

value.title: The same graph gives the same layout
value.statement: A complete layout is a function of the graph snapshot, view settings and a stable seed, never input iteration order, a previous mode's coordinates or elapsed machine time. Hub choices, cluster centres, shared-member assignments and fan order break ties by stable graph-qualified node id. A safety-capped run is reported as incomplete, not as the reproducible finished result. Deliberate dragging and incremental live nudges are not canonical full layouts.
value.done_when: Run each mode repeatedly on the same snapshot, shuffle node and edge input order, reopen the graph and switch away and back: complete runs choose identical centres and coordinates. Two open graphs with the same local node ids remain distinct. A forced cap is visibly reported and is not marked complete.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (seeded, stable id tie-breaks); existing layout's iteration-count contract

value.title: Keep the view's existing interactions
value.statement: Hub layouts respect the visible nodes and relations, including existing similarity visibility controls, and do not reveal filtered nodes or unopened graphs. Selection, node details, spine toggles, graph switching, cross-graph links and intentional entity merging keep working; merging is applied after the spine as today. A live change keeps existing nodes steady and places new nodes with a bounded update; changing a layout explicitly may reposition them. Reading a node or moving the camera never recomputes hubs.
value.done_when: Filter a hub or one of its relations, select a shared neighbour, toggle its spine from the node panel, merge entities, open a second graph and apply a live node add. No hidden node appears, selections remain valid, every visible node has one place, and camera moves and panel reads trigger no hub computation or graph reload.
value.source: Existing graph view and node-spine behaviour; project lead 2026-11-26 (all modes)

value.title: Big graphs stay responsive
value.statement: Hub detection and layout do not block the main thread, perform an all-pairs node scan or add a graph-read round trip to open the view. Runs retain the existing 15-second safety budget up to 5,000 nodes and 30-second budget above that, expose progress and cap status, and discard stale results when the graph or requested mode changes. Repeated control changes retain only the newest pending request rather than building an unbounded queue.
value.done_when: Measure all initial modes against the same-base Normal baseline on synthetic 747-node/30-band, 1,000-node dense and 10,000-node sparse graphs with matched conditions. Record total and hub-detection time, cap status, memory and main-thread responsiveness; complete below the existing budgets, add no snapshot or similarity requests, and introduce no hub-related main-thread task over 50 ms. Rapid mode changes followed by a graph switch show only the latest result and a bounded pending queue.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (big-graph speed); PR #58, PR #71; components/use-layout.ts safety budgets

value.title: Choose how many hubs to show
value.statement: A keyboard-accessible Hubs count setting selects up to that many eligible centres, defaults to 10 and is adjustable from 1 to 100. Degree mode selects the highest-ranked candidates; Similarity mode selects the strongest cluster centres. A graph with fewer eligible hubs shows only those it has; increasing the setting never invents or duplicates a node.
value.done_when: On a fixture with more than ten eligible centres, the default selects ten, changing Hubs to three selects three, and a reload keeps three. A graph with two eligible centres still shows only two at a setting of ten; out-of-range or fractional stored settings restore the default.
value.source: Project lead 2026-11-26 (the X most connected, default 10, adjustable)

value.question: How many hubs should the view select, and how should similarity influence degree ranking and the initial mode?
value.default: Select up to ten centres and assign a shared neighbour to the highest-ranked eligible hub.
value.answer: Project lead 2026-11-26: add an adjustable Hubs count, default 10; rank by degree but favour nodes central to a similarity cluster when data exists, otherwise plain degree. Keep Degree hubs and Similarity hubs separate, initially choose Similarity hubs, and fall back to Degree hubs (Most connections), not Normal, when similarity data is absent. Prime approved a bounded 25% centrality boost. Shared neighbours keep a deterministic primary fan.

value.question: Should similarity clustering follow the existing cluster-resolution slider, and which served similarity score should supply a link's weight?
value.default: Reuse the current resolution setting on the available similarity links, with the served whole-node pair score when present and equal weights otherwise. Without similarity links or usable data, fall back to Degree hubs using Most connections and show a small note, as answered in q-01; add no backend computation.

value.change: First draft. PRD-only review precedes implementation; rule-provenance integration is explicitly deferred.

Answered q-01: adjustable Hubs count defaults to 10; similarity-centrality preference with plain-degree fallback; separate modes with Similarity hubs as the initial choice. Added hub-13 and amended hub-01, hub-04 and hub-05. All delivery states remain planned.

Recorded approval and initial UI delivery: controls, Normal, Degree and Similarity selection, the declared preview, reproducible rigid fans and adjustable hub count. Spacing, spine, existing-interaction and full performance acceptance evidence remains in progress; real fill provenance remains deferred. Aligned q-02's default fallback with the answered q-01.
